ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (dark grey/black) background comprising approximately 92% of the visible surface, with high-intensity (white/light grey) pixel clusters representing approximately 8% of the surface area.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Primary dark pigmentation layer interspersed with numerous high-contrast white linear streaks and circular rosettes. White clusters are most densely concentrated at the extreme distal tips of both lobes, while linear markings are randomly oriented across the central and medial regions.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: V-shaped central notch with an approximate interior angle of 90 degrees; depth is roughly 12% of the total vertical height of the visible fluke.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, irregular serration pattern along the entire continuous boundary; pixel-amplitude of peaks and valleys varies between 2 and 15 pixels relative to the mean edge trajectory.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Upward convex curvature initiating from the medial notch and extending to the distal tips, with a sharp increase in positive slope in the lateral quadrants.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Distinct clusters of high-contrast white circular pixel groups (rosettes) measuring 5-20 pixels in diameter, located prominently at the lateral distal points of both lobes.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Dense network of multidirectional, unaligned white linear features (rake marks) of varying pixel-lengths (10-150 pixels) crossing the dark ventral pigmentation.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive white scarring consisting of both linear rake marks and circular rosette patterns (likely barnacle-related) across the entirety of the dark ventral surface.
other_distinctive_markers: The lateral tips of both lobes show extreme pixel-intensity transition from black to white due to heavy localized scarring/colonization.
